source.credit: Levison et al. (2023), ACM abstract 2184; Levison et al. (2025), Space Science Reviews 221, 70

constraints.axisConvention: Full axes are halved exactly. +Z is the adopted pole; +X is the arbitrary display meridian.
constraints.qualification: Published approximate ellipsoid from six stellar occultations, assuming the satellite's orbit is circular and equatorial.
constraints.scale: The reference radius is the geometric mean of the approximation semiaxes. It is a rendering scale, not an independent measured mean radius or convex-model volume.

assumptions: Published approximate ellipsoid from six stellar occultations, assuming the satellite's orbit is circular and equatorial.
The fitted pole assumes an equatorial satellite orbit. Rotation period and current longitude remain unqualified; the display meridian is arbitrary.
approximation.qualification: Observation-constrained ellipsoid; no invented local terrain or albedo.

spin.meaning: The fitted pole assumes an equatorial satellite orbit. Rotation period and current longitude remain unqualified; the display meridian is arbitrary.

unresolved: The selected model does not establish a current rotational phase or an unambiguous period.
